import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Set up the figure with multiple subplots for comprehensive analysis
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 12))
fig.suptitle('Titanic Survival Analysis', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)

# Color palette for survival
survival_palette = {0: '#e74c3c', 1: '#2ecc71'}
survival_labels = {0: 'Did not survive', 1: 'Survived'}

# Plot 1: Survival rate by passenger class and sex
ax1 = axes[0, 0]
survival_by_class_sex = df.groupby(['pclass', 'sex'])['survived'].mean().unstack()
survival_by_class_sex.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax1, color=['#3498db', '#e91e63'], edgecolor='black', width=0.7)
ax1.set_xlabel('Passenger Class', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_ylabel('Survival Rate', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_title('Survival Rate by Class and Sex', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_xticklabels(['1st Class', '2nd Class', '3rd Class'], rotation=0)
ax1.legend(title='Sex', loc='upper right')
ax1.set_ylim(0, 1)
for container in ax1.containers:
    ax1.bar_label(container, fmt='%.2f', fontsize=9)

# Plot 2: Age distribution by survival status
ax2 = axes[0, 1]
for survived in [0, 1]:
    subset = df[df['survived'] == survived]['age'].dropna()
    ax2.hist(subset, bins=30, alpha=0.6, label=survival_labels[survived], 
             color=survival_palette[survived], edgecolor='black', linewidth=0.5)
ax2.set_xlabel('Age', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_ylabel('Count', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_title('Age Distribution by Survival Status', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.legend(loc='upper right')

# Plot 3: Survival count by embarkation point
ax3 = axes[1, 0]
embark_survival = df.groupby(['embark_town', 'survived']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
embark_survival.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax3, color=[survival_palette[0], survival_palette[1]], 
                     edgecolor='black', width=0.7)
ax3.set_xlabel('Embarkation Town', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_ylabel('Number of Passengers', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_title('Survival Count by Embarkation Point', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_xticklabels(ax3.get_xticklabels(), rotation=45, ha='right')
ax3.legend([survival_labels[0], survival_labels[1]], title='Outcome', loc='upper right')

# Plot 4: Fare distribution by survival (violin plot)
ax4 = axes[1, 1]
df_fare = df[df['fare'] < 200].copy()  # Remove extreme outliers for better visualization
df_fare['survival_status'] = df_fare['survived'].map(survival_labels)
sns.violinplot(data=df_fare, x='survival_status', y='fare', ax=ax4, 
               palette=[survival_palette[0], survival_palette[1]], inner='box')
ax4.set_xlabel('Survival Status', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_ylabel('Fare (£)', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_title('Fare Distribution by Survival Status\n(Fares < £200)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# Add overall statistics as text
total_passengers = len(df)
survived_count = df['survived'].sum()
survival_rate = survived_count / total_passengers * 100

# Adjust layout
plt.tight_layout()

# Add a footnote with key statistics
fig.text(0.5, -0.02, f'Total Passengers: {total_passengers} | Survivors: {survived_count} | Overall Survival Rate: {survival_rate:.1f}%', 
         ha='center', fontsize=11, style='italic', color='#555555')

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
